notes: Second full audit, covering everything since feeb9a8 (rounds 2-5) and the first push to GitHub. Static Next.js export: no backend, no auth, no forms, no database, no payments, no AI calls, no analytics. Checked: (1) secrets: none in the working tree or in git history (no .env, key, certificate or credential file was ever committed); .gitignore hardened before the push to cover keys/certificates (*.pem *.key *.crt *.p12 *.pfx *.jks), credential files (.npmrc .netrc *credentials* service-account*.json), host tooling (.vercel .wrangler .netlify .aws .terraform, *.tfstate) and editor/OS noise; no tracked file is caught by the new rules. (2) injection: the only dangerouslySetInnerHTML is components/seo/JsonLd.tsx, which escapes < before serialising; no eval, no new Function, no innerHTML; the six client components (lyrics dialog, lightbox, copy-email, two embed facades, language switcher) render server-passed children and never build markup from strings. (3) content validation: every URL in content/ now goes through httpUrl (zod, protocol pinned to http/https); SiteSchema.url was the one field still on bare z.url(), which in zod 4 accepts javascript: and data:, and is now pinned as well; gallery keys are constrained to /^[a-z0-9-]+$/ and checked against the image manifest at build. (4) deployment: public/_headers keeps CSP (script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline', unavoidable for a static export that inlines RSC payloads; no unsafe-eval; frame-src limited to youtube-nocookie.com and bandcamp.com; object-src none; base-uri self; form-action self; frame-ancestors none), HSTS preload, nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP; the stale 'no eval needed for three.js' note was corrected since three.js is gone; the production build emits no browser source maps and only out/ is deployed. (5) CI: both workflows now declare least-privilege GITHUB_TOKEN scopes (contents: read for CI, permissions: {} for the weekly rebuild); the Cloudflare deploy hook is read from a repository secret into an env var and never echoed. (6) third parties: YouTube and Bandcamp load only after a click, nothing is stored, external links carry rel=noopener. (7) dependencies: npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities in production dependencies; 7 advisories remain in dev-only tooling (extract-zip, qs, tmp, uuid, via the lighthouse and serve chains), none reachable at runtime and none fixable without a breaking change. Findings: no Critical, no High. Medium: SiteSchema.url accepted any URL scheme (fixed). Low: unconstrained gallery image keys (fixed), unscoped workflow token permissions (fixed), CSP relies on 'unsafe-inline' for scripts (documented, inherent to static export), the booking address is published in plain text in the Impressum (required by German law, accepted), dev-dependency advisories to revisit at the next tooling update. Round 6 delta audit (hero player, painted dividers, retimed background): the one new surface is components/music/HeroPlayer.tsx, a third client component embedding Bandcamp. Its iframe URL is assembled only from content/site.json heroTrack.bandcampTrackId, which the schema pins to /^\d+$/, so nothing user-supplied can reach the src; the release slug is a slug regex and the title is cross-checked at build against that record's own tracklist. The embed origin https://bandcamp.com is already the only Bandcamp host in the CSP frame-src allowlist, the frame carries referrerPolicy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and nothing is requested before an explicit click with the consent line and a link to the privacy policy shown first. The divider assets (rule-brush.webp, edge-deckle.webp and its mirror) are static images generated from the sleeve and are used only as CSS masks. No new dependency, no new network origin, no new form, storage or script. Findings: no Critical, no High, no Medium. Low: the Bandcamp iframe carries no sandbox attribute, matching the existing Bandcamp and YouTube facades; it loads only on consent from an allowlisted origin, and tightening it would need testing against the player's own requirements. Round 8 delta audit (GitHub Pages deployment). New file .github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml. (1) Permissions are least-privilege per job: build has contents:read plus pages:write and id-token:write, deploy has only pages:write and id-token:write; nothing has contents:write. The build job needs pages:write solely for configure-pages' enablement call. (2) No script injection: the step that derives the base path reads $GITHUB_REPOSITORY as a shell environment variable rather than interpolating ${{ }} inside a run block, which is the injection vector. (3) Triggers are push-on-main and workflow_dispatch only; there is no pull_request or pull_request_target trigger, so no fork can run it. (4) No secrets are referenced. (5) Only first-party actions/* are used. (6) The three build variables are NEXT_PUBLIC_* by design: they are public URLs, and nothing secret is inlined. (7) The published artifact is out/, the same public static site; the preview is deliberately noindex (robots.txt disallows all, every page carries robots: noindex) so it cannot compete with brickwater.de. Findings: no Critical, no High. Medium: GitHub Pages sends no custom headers, so the CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy in public/_headers do not apply to the preview; this is a real loss of defence in depth versus the Cloudflare target, accepted because the preview is a static site with no cookies, no storage, no forms, no auth and no third-party script before an explicit click, and it is documented in GO-LIVE.md section 6. Low: actions are pinned to major tags rather than commit SHAs, consistent with the repo's existing workflows.
